Snapchat mobile application forensics

A comparative investigation of Snapchat artefacts across Android and iOS environments.

01

Project introduction

Snapchat stores its data in application databases that differ between platforms. This investigation compared what could be recovered from an Android phone and an iPhone using the same approach.

Academic case studyNames, usernames, emails and device identifiers from the exercise are withheld. All illustrations are labelled.

03

Investigation objective

Uncover the structure, behaviour and functionality of Snapchat on iOS and Android using Cellebrite Physical Analyzer.

04

Background and context

Snapchat is a messaging application with features aimed at privacy, such as My Eyes Only, so it is a useful case for showing how application design shapes what remains on a device.

What is a write-ahead log?

A database writes changes to a separate log before applying them to the main file. The log can hold recent changes that are not yet in the database. The Snapchat database log was about 4 MB on Android and about 2 MB on iOS.

05

Evidence sources

  • Android. Full file system extraction (legacy extraction type) of a Samsung SM-G986B.
  • iOS. Full file system extraction of an iPhone.
06

Tools and technologies

Cellebrite Physical AnalyzerMagnet AXIOM
07

Acquisition methodology

Hash values were noted before extraction so they could be compared after analysis. A matching hash shows the examination did not change the extracted data.

  • RecoveredContacts. Android showed 4 Snapchat contacts out of 10. iOS showed 3 out of 6.
  • RecoveredMedia on Android. 6,212 images, of which 1,241 were Snapchat images. 24 videos, of which 11 were Snapchat.
  • RecoveredMedia on iOS. 94 videos in the examined directory, of which 3 were Snapchat.
  • RecoveredMessages. 26 conversation rows in the database view, matching the message artefact. The report notes signs of deleted messages.
  • ConfirmedIntegrity. Hash values at the start and end matched on both devices.
  • InterpretationReport interpretation. The report reads the iOS result as showing that iOS is harder to extract Snapchat data from. This is a reading of one comparison, not a general rule.
10

Visual evidence gallery

The original screenshots in this report contain account names, emails and device identifiers, so only a cropped example is shown.

11

Limitations and challenges

  • LimitationNot all data could be extracted. The report states that not every item can be recovered with Cellebrite.
  • LimitationPlatform differences. Snapchat-specific stores appeared on Android and not on iOS, so the two results are not like for like.
  • LimitationExtraction type. Both extractions were of the legacy type.
  • LimitationUnreported categories. Location, browser, settings and cloud areas were examined but no results are documented.
12

Technical skills demonstrated

Android analysisiOS analysisSQLite application databasesWrite-ahead logsHash verificationCross-platform comparison
13

Final investigative takeaway

The same app leaves different evidence on different platforms, so findings from one cannot be assumed for the other.

iOS gave richer device-level details. Android gave more Snapchat-specific stores. Matching hash values support that the examination did not alter the data.
